evidence: Kew/POWO and USDA/Forest Service sources accept Echinacea angustifolia as native in Texas.
Hays County — the project Hays County native-source list includes E. angustifolia.
NPSOT treats the species as a Central/West Texas native of prairies, meadows, pastures and woodland edges.
USDA ecological-site material documents E. angustifolia as a native component in Texas prairie systems, but the reviewed page does not itself lock a second and third exact project county.
Bell/Williamson-area records found in B016 include landscaping, transplant, sale, or seed-mix contexts and are therefore not counted as native county evidence.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: B016 did not recover three exact target-zone counties with native/wild evidence independent of planting or restoration use. The species is Texas-native, but the project threshold remains unmet in this review.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not convert Fort Cavazos landscaping lists, Balcones Canyonlands transplants, nursery-sale lists, or TxDOT seed mixes into native-county occurrence. Keep cultivated E. purpurea/pallida comparisons separate from target-zone nativity.

morphology.look_here_first: Ignore ray color first. Look for the combination of very narrow rough leaves and a usually single head on a stout little-branched stem, with drooping rays around a hard prickly cone.
diagnostic_traits: deep-rooted perennial from a stout woody taproot/crown rather than a spreading rhizomatous colony
stems stout and usually simple or only weakly branched, often bearing one head
basal and cauline leaves narrow linear-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, much longer than wide
leaf margins mostly entire; surfaces conspicuously rough/hairy
heads radiate with pink-purple ray florets often reflexed or drooping
central disk is strongly conical and prickly because of stiff chaff/bracts among the disk florets
fruit a cypsela; pappus much reduced compared with fluffy mistflowers/snakeroots

confusers.separator: Prairie coneflower has an elongated columnar disk and deeply divided leaves; Echinacea angustifolia has narrow mostly entire rough leaves and a shorter broad conical prickly disk.
Purple coneflower usually has much broader ovate leaves and a more branched/rhizomatous garden habit; do not use flower color alone.
Pale coneflower can have very drooping rays and narrow leaves; use phyllary/chaff details, leaf pubescence, and verified range rather than ray droop alone.

diagnostic_roles: side-profile head showing drooping rays and prickly cone

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project-native until three target-zone counties are documented or Calvin explicitly approves a documented exception.
